To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

particle-based variational inference (ParVI) methods can be understood as a smoothing treatment of the true Wasserstein gradient flow, that this smoothing treatment is essentially in either of two forms, and that the two forms can be used to develop acceleration methods and a bandwidth-selection method for ParVIs.

we (1) unify various existing ParVIs by a novel understanding of their finite-particle approximation, (2) propose a general acceleration framework for ParVIs based on this understanding, (3) propose a principled bandwidth selection method for ParVIs that leverages the geometry of the underlying Wasserstein space, and (4) demonstrate the benefits of our methods in a series of experiments on both synthetic and real-world data.
